hypotheses.text: The health-check endpoint returned HTTP 200 (E10) but the JSON body's /status field contained "degraded" instead of the required "ok" (E3). The jsonPointer /status was present (missingJsonPointer is null) and the jsonEquals predicate matched the wrong value, so this is an application-level behavior mismatch rather than a transport or schema-structure failure. The baseline marked the assertion step as "different" (chain[1]), indicating the prior successful run observed /status=="ok" while this run observed /status=="degraded". This is consistent with the service reporting a degraded internal health state while still accepting HTTP connections and returning 2xx. The HTTP 200 status alone is not proof of a root cause; however, the required-true assertion on the response body value, combined with the prior passing baseline, grounds an observed product-behavior mismatch. No source-code handles were supplied, so the specific code path or dependency that flipped health to "degraded" cannot be identified from this evidence set.
